key_insight: A proposed universal scaling law links droplet projection area to key impact loads, capturing the influence of initial shape and orientation.
engineering_relevance: Accounting for non-spherical droplet impacts could improve wind turbine leading-edge erosion predictions and maintenance planning.
method: Couple incompressible multiphase flow simulations with finite element analysis of blade materials.
Investigate impact dynamics across arbitrary droplet shapes and orientations.
Relate impact loading metrics to initial droplet projection area.
evidence_signal: Simulations show positively correlated peak pressure, loaded area at peak pressure, and peak force, while peak-force timing scales inversely; the abstract reports no quantitative errors or experimental validation.
watch_item: The proposed law needs validation across realistic rain and sea-spray conditions before use in erosion-life predictions.
paper_title: Influence of Droplet Morphology on Fluid Dynamics and Impact Erosion of Wind Turbine Blades
